tagline: A local call-graph index so coding agents query code instead of repeating grep and read

scenes.narration: Day 60: codegraph, a local call graph index that lets a coding agent query code in one shot instead of repeating grep and read.

scenes.heading: What is it?
bullets: Indexes functions, classes and call edges into local SQLite
Serves lookups to agents over MCP or a CLI
No API key, no GPU, fully local
scenes.narration: Codegraph scans a repo, builds a call graph, and lets an agent ask one query instead of repeating grep and read.

steps.narration: We ran this on our own 159 file repo. Init parsed every file and wrote 2,162 nodes and 4,700 edges to local SQLite in 2.6 seconds.
Callers traced correctly across files, even through a renamed JavaScript export alias, something grep alone misses.
But a query only matches the original declared name, and it only follows call edges, never meaning.

scenes.heading: What we found
scenes.caption: Two functions with identical validation logic but no call relationship shared zero graph edges.
scenes.narration: We wrote two functions with identical logic but no shared calls. Impact and callers found zero connection between them, confirming a real limit: duplicate logic is invisible without a call edge.
